   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  April 10, 2025

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Secretary Pelayo

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Secretary Cynthia Esquivel and Commissioner Edgar Pelayo.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, and Parks Superintendent
Glenn Massey.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident: CDBG has one million dollars for Parks projects; will be
attending future meetings.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. POLICE DEPARTMENT ORAL REPORT REGARDING CITY PARK SAFETY
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel.
Director Costley introduced Lt. Carlos Correa, who explained how the Police Department has extra patrols
at SG Park because of the high volume of visitors. Not many major incidents during the Azaez festival,
carnival, or car show; a discussion ensued.
Vice Chair Ruiz stated that a neighbor is concerned with gang members hanging out at the outdoor
restrooms, can call to the PD be on the City’s app? Lt. Correa replied yes, but crime in progress should be
called in to 911. How about drinking at Sofive; by the time the PD arrives they are gone. Director Costley
explained that the Park rules are posted up around the park and in the brochure. Chair Flores asked for a
quarterly report from the PD

2. REVIEW OF CONCESSION AGREEMENTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Commissioner Pelayo asked if Vet Care is the
only vendor doing pet vaccinations in the City, Director Costley stated that yes, the different vendors don’t
like to come in when there’s already an established vendor. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if they do spaying or
neutering? Director Costley: not on site, no room for the vehicle. Commissioner Pelayo asked if other
Partner Organizations are doing the Snack Bar? Director Costley: no, they are only open after 3pm
weekdays and on Saturdays.

3. REVIEW OF PARKS & RECREATION REVENUES
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked what Quimby fees?
Director Costley: they are fees charged to builders to offset costs at parks due to the impact of more
people using them. Chair Flores proposed selling advertising space on the fences

4. PARK FACILITY MAINTENANCE DIVISION ANNUAL REPORT
  Page 1 of 2
  4
 Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/ Commissioner Pelayo
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

5. PROPOSED PROGRAM FEES FOR 2025/2026
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the Proposed Program Fee Schedule for May 11, 2025.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Chair Flores asked if the Golf Course fee will be
increased

6. PROCURING SHADE FOR DIAMONDS NINE & TEN - ORAL REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel
Deputy Dir. De La Rosa reviewed this item; staff is working on getting quotes; a discussion ensued.
Commissioner Pelayo stated he’s looking forward to the completed project.

7. ORAL REPORT REGARDING COMMISSION UPDATE REQUESTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo
Deputy Dir. De La Rosa reviewed this item, the survey is still ongoing, posted at all Paks facilities and at
events. Repairs on the batting cages have started; a discussion ensued.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Circle Park will be completed by the end of May. We expect the Urban Orchard
completion date to be mid-July.

Deputy Dir. De La Rosa: Staff had a busy month of March with the Azalea Festival; all the events were
successful. A temporary pickle ball court has been set up in one of the tennis courts. Mentioned upcoming
special events.

Parks Supt. Massey: Staff has been trimming trees around playgrounds at SG Parks. Also, overseeding
projects at all parks. Ball fields and soccer fields have been renovated.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: No comments at this time.

Commissioner Pelayo: No comments at this time.

Commissioner Flores: Wanted to know if the travel team issues have been resolved, Deputy Dir. De La Rosa
stated the team has disbanded.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:15 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary
Parks & Recreation Commission

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Secretary Esquivel

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant

different aspects of aquatics and customer service.

2. THIRD QUARTER REVIEW OF RECREATION PROGRAMS FY 2024/25
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.

Deputy Dir. De La Rosa reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Secretary Esquivel stated that there was a
misunderstanding with the oft play area that kids needed wristbands. Commissioner Pelayo asked if there
are special needs classes; no but programs are inclusive. Secretary Esquivel suggestd sending out staff to
the baseball games with the Parks QR survey code. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if classes will be given at
Hollydale Community Park.

3. THIRD QUARTER REVIEW OF GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE FY 2024/25

M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Chair Flores thanked staff for their hard work. Vice Chair Ruiz agreed with Chair Flores. Commissioner
Pelayo mentioned that there’s a bent volleyball pole; Parks Supt. Massey replied that it has already been
repaired.

4. PROPOSED PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE 2025/26

  6
 Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and the proposed meeting schedule with any suggested
changes for the coming fiscal year.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo to approve the proposed meeting schedule with the changes
suggested by Chair Flores.
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Chair Flores suggested adding a PD safety report
in April and November.

5. ANNUAL PARTNER ORGANIZATION REPORTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the Proposed Program Fee Schedule for May 11, 2025.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Pelayo
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz stated that staff has been very
helpful to the Aztecs Football team, and in her opinion doesn’t see any gratitude from them.
Commissioner Pelayo asked what is the City’s roll in assisting the Aztecs; Director Costley described how
the Department has helped them. He also mentioned he would like to see a more detailed report from the
JAA; Director Costley will look into standardizing a form.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Memorial Day Ceremony will be Saturday, May 24. The Tweedy Mile Street Fair will start
June 6; Men’s Health Fair is June 7, and staff is preparing for July 4.

Deputy Dir. De La Rosa: The Mom Prom event was very successful; May 3 was the JAA’s Opening Day and
kick off for the art exhibit ¡Jugamos! Special Olympics will be at SG Park on May 31; June 11 will be a new
event Summer Kick Off, Aquatics will have their Kick Off on June 14. The Annual Spring Fit 5K is Saturday
with over 900 participants. June 18 the Golf Course will host a tournament.

Parks Supt. Massey: Staff is preparing for the 5K on Saturday and getting the parks ready for summer.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Secretary Esquivel: Asked if everyone had received the email sent out by a resident concerning JAA field
issues. Director Costley did not receive it; a discussion ensued. Secretary Esquivel will forward the email to
staff to forward to Director Costley.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS
Commissioner Pelayo asked for a report regarding the Quimby fees be brought at a future meeting.

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:46 p.m. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  August 14, 2025
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  July 26, 2025

Subject:  Review of Recreation Programs 4th Quarter FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The fourth quarter traditionally marks the beginning of peak season at the Swim
Stadium, and while we did experience growth during this season, we also went through
some ebbs and flows due to staffing issues, potential budget cuts, and external factors.

Participation in our Learn-to-Swim program, which runs from March through November,
grew steadily through April and May, with its usual surge in June when the weather gets
warmer and the kids exit school. However, the start of summer wasn’t as strong as
previous years’ due to staffing issues, we couldn't offer morning group swim lessons or
as many evening group lessons, and due to potential budget cuts, we dropped our
Friday private & semi-private swim lessons. The ongoing immigration-related issues
also negatively impacted our registration numbers and attendance to our recreational
swim sessions. Nonetheless, almost 1,400 individuals enrolled during this period,
including almost 930 in group lessons, nearly 230 in private sessions, and another 230
in semi-private lessons. We maintained steady enrollment across all age groups,
enrolling 130 Parent & Child participants (ages 6 months–2 years), 359 Tiny Tots (ages
3–5), 810 Youth (ages 6–17), and 75 Adults (18 and older). June also marked the
launch of seasonal programs such as Splash Swim Camp, Gator Swim Academy,
Junior Lifeguards, Junior Water Polo, and Surfing 101. We have almost 100 participants
thus far in these programs and expect them to keep growing.

Spring/early summer also featured various special events and programs at the pool. In
April, the Aquatics Team was excited to launch our first ever Easter Splash Fest! This
event featured an underwater and patio area egg hunt, easter bunny-shaped bounce
house, bunny photo ops, and more. We had over 220 participants register for this event.
We were also very honored to participate in local elementary schools’ Career Day,
where we taught kids about the lifeguarding profession, gave CPR demos, and talked

  Page 1 of 5

  8
 about the importance of being water safe. In May we proudly accepted the "May is
Water Safety Month" proclamation and celebrated with the Water Safety Bash. The
Swim Stadium hosted several more key events during this period: Youth & Adult Swim
Clinic, World’s Largest Swimming Lesson, and the first of three free Community Swim
Days (Summer Kick-Off) all supported by partner organization SGAC and attended by
almost 200 people. Four swim meets were hosted during the quarter, including the
South-Central Swim League's Spring Championship, with each meet drawing close to
400 swimmers and their families. Proceeds from concessions supported our partner,
SGAC. We also conducted a Lifeguard Certification class, hired six of the graduates,
and offered an Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED course attended by 10
individuals. Our annual Lifeguard Recertification took place, successfully renewing
certifications for almost 40 returning staff members.

Lastly, we saw a slight increase in membership sign-ups, particularly for our Splash
Fitness program, thanks to the 2nd Annual Aqua Fitness Expo, where attendees could
try out various aquatic fitness classes. Aquatic fitness classes’ attendance remained
steady. Private rentals picked up, with the month of June being fully booked. We
couldn't expand our morning hours due to staff shortages, but we did bring back the
popular "Moonlight Lagoon," the 9-9:45pm adults-only swim session. Finally, our facility
continues to serve as the training hub for three swim teams: SGAC, Penguins Aquatic
Club, and Lynwood Marlins, collectively engaging nearly 300 young swimmers.

Fitness
Total Fitness memberships sold or renewed during the 4th Quarter dropped to
approximately 2,500, a decrease from the 4,100 recorded in the previous quarter.
Premier Memberships declined from 800 to about 600 active members, while
Sports/Splash Memberships currently total around 450. The reduction in active
memberships is attributed to the Department's transition to a new credit card processing
system, which now supports Tap to Pay functionality.
Sports Center check-ins for the quarter reached approximately 19,000 in the 3rd quarter.
Fitness daily admissions totaled around 800, while Sports daily admissions came in at
approximately 2,500. The absence of the Junior Athletic Association’s indoor basketball
season during this period allowed for more open gym availability, contributing to the
steady usage of the facility for recreational play.

The Personal Training program saw a 165% increase in the number of packages sold
this quarter, while total training hours delivered remained consistent. This trend aligns
with seasonal patterns, as warmer weather typically drives higher interest in fitness
services. The Private 12-session package continued to be the most popular offering,
followed by the Semi-Private 16-session option.

The Annual Spring Fit 5K took place on May 10, marking the 8 th year of the event. Once
again Bimbo was the title sponsor and provided the race shirts. The race welcomed
over 950 participants and more than 300 spectators. The Spring Fit 5K remains our
largest race of the year, setting the stage for the upcoming Fun Run in July. The vendor
fair accompanying the event was a major highlight, featuring raffle give-a-ways
sponsored by Raising Cane’s and Bimbo, while Northgate Markets provided water
bottles and fresh fruit for participants.
Lastly, Fitness staff participated in the Summer Kick-Off event on Thursday, June 11,
  Page 2 of 5

  9
 from 3-7pm. The event invited community members to explore Parks and Recreation
programs and services. Fitness hosted an outdoor Zumba session and operated a
promotional booth, alongside other Divisions, as part of the Department’s family-friendly
showcase.

Youth Sports:
All youth Fundamental Sports Classes offered during the spring session experienced
exceptionally high demand, reaching full capacity within just a few days of registration.
The popularity of the spring session is largely attributed to the favorable weather, which
creates optimal conditions for outdoor sports. Attendance remained consistent
throughout the duration of the program, and participants received completion certificates
on the final day of class.

During Spring Break (April 14–18), coaches facilitated a weeklong Sports Camp,
featuring a different sport each day, including soccer, flag football, volleyball, basketball,
and baseball. Each participant received a South Gate Sports Camp T-shirt, along with a
newly designed, custom sack pack.
Summer registration opened on June 9 and reached full capacity within hours, even
after increasing class sizes to 25 participants. This remains our most popular session,
primarily due to the availability offered by the summer break. Classes are currently in
progress and will conclude on August 21. The Youth Sports staff continue to
demonstrate excellence in instruction, with a strong emphasis on skill development and
maximizing player performance in every class.

Adult Sports:
The fourth quarter commenced with the conclusion of registration for the Spring Adult
Softball season. This season included three men’s divisions and, for the first time, four
coed divisions. At the end of the season, seven division champions were crowned and
awarded redesigned Championship hoodies in addition to their trophies. A total of 40
teams competed across all seven divisions. Looking ahead, the fall season is scheduled
to span 10 weeks and will conclude with playoffs.

During summer break, open play volleyball has continued to be one of the most well-
attended weekly activities, particularly on Tuesday evenings. In response to the
increasing demand, the department will host its inaugural Volleyball After Dark event on
July 29. Interest remains strong, with both new and returning players consistently
attending to engage in multiple pick-up games. This site remains one of the few
locations in the area to offer open play volleyball. Additionally, staff are actively
recruiting for the upcoming Men’s and Women’s Basketball and Volleyball leagues, with
the goal of launching league play in the fall.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
The SG Aztecs continued their pre-season football and cheer practices at Hollydale
Regional Park. Additionally, they participated once again in the Spring Fit 5K, hosting an
informational and recruitment booth that allowed them to engage with the community in
non-traditional fashion.

SGJAA hosted their Spring Baseball/Softball Opening Day on Saturday, May 3. The
event featured festive baseball-themed music, a team parade across the field, and a
  Page 3 of 5

  10
 welcome address by JAA organization board members, who expressed their
appreciation for the community’s ongoing support. Clinton Yates from ESPN radio was
an honorary guest and delivered words of encouragement for all the athletes. The
celebration concluded with complimentary hot dogs, chips, and beverages for all
attendees. Meanwhile, registration for the Summer Basketball season began, with team
practices commencing shortly thereafter.

AYSO successfully concluded its spring season on July 26 and is now preparing for the
upcoming fall season, set to begin in September. Online registration is currently open
for those interested in participating.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 5,645. In the last quarter we had 6 posts and 146
stories. We have reached over 28,000 accounts and engaged with over 2,144. Our
new Recreation Marketing Coordinator oversees the Social Media Task Force and all
social media outlets.

Senior Center
Spring at the Senior Center was full steam ahead, filled with memorable events, excursions and
programming. Our goal is to promote community engagement and enrich the lives of our senior
residents by providing endless opportunities. In April, the Senior Center celebrated Easter with
a vibrant gathering that included treats, decorations, and social activities. Seniors enjoyed a
festive Easter party featuring: a fun-filled egg hunt that brought joy and laughter. Each attendee
received an assortment of Easter-themed treats, played interactive games and participated in
activities that fostered connection amongst the participants. May was a month dedicated to
honoring our beloved mothers. The Mothers Day celebration included a beautifully decorated
event where seniors gathered to celebrate. Each registered senior received a thoughtful gift,
ensuring every mother felt cherished. A variety of treats, along with games and activities tailored
to celebrate motherhood. June highlighted our appreciation for fathers with a dedicated
celebration with a delightful gathering. With a special performance by Mariachi Los Angeles our
seniors were able to sing, dance, and celebrate together in the festive atmosphere.

Spring also provided our registered seniors with a new series of exciting excursions, which
included visits to local casinos, LA County Fair, Temecula Balloon & Wine festival, Hollywood
Bowl, and Disney on Ice.

Contract/Youth Classes:
Spring contract class operations continued with our core offerings: baby boogie, baby Mexican
folk, ballet, tumbling, tap, hip hop, cheer, and creative dance. Classes worked persistently for 8
weeks to get up on stage and perform their routines at our culminating dance recitals. To
accommodate all classes and their families, we added in an additional recital and hosted three
evening recitals in total. Each night hosted 500 observers per show, you could feel the energy
from the performances.

Our Tiny Two’s and Tot Time classes were able to go on an excursion. Each class had the
opportunity to go to the LA County Fair complete with a class presentation in the garden and
farmhouse prior to entry.

Lil Chefs, our 5-week program was again at maximum capacity, with two classes being offered
on Tuesday evenings. Students learn two new recipes per week and enjoy their hard work at

  Page 4 of 5

  11
 the end of every class. In addition to learning and cooking the recipes, students are also taught
kitchen safety and the proper handling of appliances.

Special Events:
Spring season for Special events is light regarding actual events being produced and hosted.
Memorial Day was the only event to take place and that was held on May 25. This event would
not have been possible without the assistance of our guest speaker Petty Officer 2nd class Max
Garcia, Bishop Juan Carlos Mendez, Girl Scout Ambassador Lindsey Prieto, Officer Romero,
Detective Sanchez, and the South Gate Explorers. Attendees were welcomed with our
Memorial Day Program and light refreshments.

Although there were not many events to host during this quarter, the planning for the remainder
of the year started. Staff worked effortlessly to find new musical talent to bring to this year’s
Concerts in the Park. After searching the Concert series was finalized: Corazon de Mana, Los
Del Momento, Grupo Neblina, and Mariachi Divas were selected. Movies in the Park were also
planned, staff made their selections and narrowed the list down to 5 movies: Kung Fu Panda 4,
Haunted Mansion, Trolls, Wonka, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

Cultural Arts:
Home Town Hero was the group art exhibit for the spring, this exhibit celebrated artist’s local
hero or hero’s. Our team was also able to display Dream: South Gate Senior High’s Art Show
which was a mixture of teens from freshman to seniors. For the opening we had artists, artisans,
vendors, and activities for everyone to enjoy. We designated a section of the museum to also
shine light on Hometown heroes throughout South Gate’s History. The exhibit was open for a
total of 9 weeks, many visitors came through the door to view and enjoy the terrific submissions
that were on display. On June 1 the team celebrated the closing of Home Town Hero and South
Gate Senior High’s Dream.

Not only is our museum team busy with internal programming, but they also have the
opportunity to collaborate with many other organizations. First, museum staff were invited to the
Legacy Complex for their annual Wellness Fair where they provided a watercolor activity to
promote self-care. Second, the team also started to gear up with social assets to highlight
LGBTQ+ identifying artists in celebration of Pride Month. We completed PRIDE MONTH:
LGBTQ+ Historical events & figures zine Volume 2 and will be providing copies at South East
High Schools Pride Festival. We also were able to guide the community through a watercolor
activity at Pride Fest. Lastly, our team also provided a collage button making activity to guests at
the Chicxs Rockerxs SELA Swapmeet & Greet in celebration and promotion of our new open
call Oír de Nuevo – Press Repeat. AAPI (Asian American & Pacific Islander) Heritage month
was in full celebration with a curated playlist and artists highlighted throughout the month of
May.

Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat open call submissions closed Sunday, June 9 so the curation
began that following week. The museum team has been organizing and creating promotional
goods for Zine Fiesta 3 that we will host on Saturday, August 10 in conjunction with the opening
reception of Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  July 29, 2025

Subject:  Review of Grounds & Facility Maintenance 4th Quarter FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance Activities
  • The Golf Course greens were aerated.
  • Four ball washing stations were repaired.
  • Southern Avenue Parks were mulched and 35 sprinklers were replaced at Cesar
  Chavez Phase Two.
  • The Golf Course putting greens were fertilized.
  • We repaired a three-inch water main break and six broken lateral irrigation lines
  at Hollydale Regional Park.
  • Staff raised sunken irrigation valve boxes throughout all City parks to prevent trip
  and fall hazards.
  • Two John Deer Tractors and a Greens mower were ordered and should be
  delivered by mid-September.
  • Staff have caught over 165 Gophers throughout all City Parks this quarter.
  • At Triangle Park we planted two Crape Myrtle trees and added mulch to make it
  more attractive and welcoming.
  • Staff are coping with the recent heat waves and syringe cycling the irrigation
  systems to add additional water to all parks to ensure the turf stays green

Park Facility Maintenance

Parks Facility Maintenance staff set up and hosted a variety of events, Earth Day at
South Gate Park, Men’s Health Fair, and Spirit Jam just to mention a few.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms. We remain vigilant when
addressing the ongoing challenges with restroom cleanliness with a routine restroom
  Page 1 of 2

  13
 disinfecting program. This includes the use of the C3 Machine to apply disinfectants and
cleaners. Once the product is sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure
sanitary conditions.

We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in
our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities,
along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools are used
consistently. Set-ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door
handles, and A/V equipment.

Additionally, we purchased a new auto scrubber to service park buildings for more
efficient cleaning and disinfecting of floors. Also, a new wheelchair lift was purchased to
replace the older broken one.

During this period, we replaced the Auditorium glass door closures making it easier and
safer to enter and exit the building.

To accommodate classes, reservations, and events, staff schedules have been
adjusted to ensure full coverage and support. Facility staff have displayed exceptional
flexibility and professionalism in managing the transition between regular operations
and new demands, consistently responding to the evolving needs of the Division.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting the intake to 15
people maximum per day.

Parks are busy with many events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. Both Grounds
Maintenance and Facility Maintenance staff work together to make sure all events run
smoothly.

Subject:  Report on Activities for Halloween

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary: This year’s Halloween Haunt events will take place at both Hollydale
Community Park on Saturday, October 25, from 6:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m. and South Gate Park on
Friday, October 31, 2025, from 6:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.

We’re thrilled to bring the Halloween spirit back to Hollydale Community Park! Our team is
brewing up a brand-new concept and an exciting itinerary that’s sure to delight. Guests can look
forward to festive game booths, trick-or-treating fun, a lively costume contest, and music from a
live DJ to keep the energy high. To top it all off, we’ll wrap up the evening with a special
Halloween-themed movie screening under the stars!

Our Halloween Haunt at South Gate Park was such a success last year with its complete re-
vamp, that we will be utilizing a similar setup and itinerary with a couple of minor modifications.
Patrons will still see our Department’s show mobile as the main stage with our festive
Halloween décor. Our annual costume contest, game booths, train rides, Halloween crafts and
DJ will also be available this year. The costume contest will be judged by members of the City
Council and Parks & Recreation Commission, who will have the challenging task of selecting
winners in three categories across all age groups. Get ready for fun and excitement as our
game booths line the outfield of Diamond 3, offering interactive challenges sure to delight
guests of all ages! Over on Diamond 4, hop aboard our train rides, running in a continuous loop
and ready to welcome 16 to 24 riders per trip. And don’t miss the music, our event DJ will keep
the energy high with a lively mix of today’s hits and classic Halloween tunes!

South Gate residents are in for a treat with an exciting new feature added to this year’s
festivities! Guests can look forward to our new “Spooky Village”, a maze of Halloween themed
canopies that will offer an efficient trick or treating experience. Inflatables will again be grouped
by age to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all, and little ones will also have their
dedicated toddler soft play area. Photo ops will be scattered throughout the event, featuring all-
new themed sets, backdrops, and an interactive photo booth that prints and texts your pictures
instantly. When it’s time to refuel, stop by our food truck area, complete with a Halloween-
themed seating zone perfect for enjoying tasty treats and sweet desserts!

Led by Recreation Coordinator Salomon Lopez, this year’s Halloween Haunt events are sure to
be a scary good time.
